content.user_title: Explain Machine Learning Models with SHAP
content.value_statement: Machine learning teams need clear reasons behind model predictions. This skill guides SHAP explainer choice, plots, debugging, fairness checks, and production explanation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable SHAP explainers for tree, deep learning, linear, and black-box models.
Shows how to compute SHAP values and interpret base values, signs, and magnitudes.
Guides waterfall, beeswarm, bar, scatter, force, heatmap, violin, and decision plots.
Supports debugging, feature engineering, model comparison, fairness analysis, and production explanation services.
Explains performance choices such as sampling, batching, and explainer caching.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a runnable package or hosted service.
It assumes the user supplies trained models, data, and relevant Python libraries.
It cannot verify whether a model explanation is causally valid.
Large datasets and black-box explainers may still be slow or costly.

use_cases.title: Debug Model Predictions
use_cases.description: Find features that drive errors, outliers, and unexpected predictions with local and global SHAP views.

use_cases.title: Prepare Model Review Evidence
use_cases.description: Create explanation plots and plain-language summaries for model validation, audits, or stakeholder review.

use_cases.title: Monitor Fairness Signals
use_cases.description: Compare SHAP patterns across groups and identify proxy features that may need mitigation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain One Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this SHAP skill to explain my trained model. Recommend the right explainer and the first plots to create.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Visualizations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this SHAP skill to choose plots for global importance, local predictions, and feature interactions. Include when to use each plot.

prompt_templates.title: Debug and Improve Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this SHAP skill to analyze model errors, detect data leakage, and suggest feature engineering steps from SHAP patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Explanations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this SHAP skill to design a production explanation workflow with caching, batch processing, latency controls, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Explain why a classifier rejected one application.
output_examples.output: A waterfall-style explanation identifies the strongest positive and negative feature contributions, then summarizes which inputs drove the final decision.
A model comparison report ranks feature importance for each model, highlights inconsistent drivers, and notes accuracy and interpretability tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Check a model for fairness issues.
output_examples.output: A fairness analysis compares SHAP values across groups, flags protected attributes and proxy features, and suggests mitigation options.

best_practices: Start with global plots, then inspect local predictions that matter to the decision.
Use representative background data and document how the baseline was chosen.
Validate SHAP insights with domain knowledge before changing features or policy.
anti_patterns: Using KernelExplainer for tree models when TreeExplainer is available.
Treating SHAP associations as causal proof without additional analysis.
Explaining very large datasets without sampling, batching, or latency planning.

faq.question: What models can this skill help explain?
faq.answer: It covers tree, deep learning, linear, and black-box models through the main SHAP explainer families.

faq.question: Does it run SHAP automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and workflows that users can apply in their own Python environment.

faq.question: Which plots does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers waterfall, beeswarm, bar, scatter, force, heatmap, violin, and decision plots.

faq.question: Can it help with fairness analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to compare SHAP patterns across groups and identify protected attributes or proxy features.

faq.question: Can it support production use?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers caching explainers, batching requests, limiting output complexity, and monitoring explanation quality.

faq.question: Are SHAP values causal explanations?
faq.answer: No. SHAP describes model behavior and feature associations. Causal claims need separate study design and evidence.
